result:
Editing the comments list is done: authors can now edit their own comments and get a "Comment Updated" notification after saving. I haven't run tests, lint or the app, as you asked.

The lint hook flagged `useNotifications` in the new component. I moved the success notification into the `useUpdateComment` hook, as `features/CLAUDE.md` requires. A search of the feature folder shows `update-comment.tsx` no longer uses `useNotifications`, so the last hook error was stale. It fired after the first of my four edits.

- **API:** `features/comments/api/update-comment.ts` sends `PATCH /comments/{commentId}` with the new `body`. It refreshes the comments list and shows the success notification.
- **Edit button:** `features/comments/components/update-comment.tsx` adds an Edit button that opens a form drawer pre-filled with the current body.
- **Comments list:** `comments-list.tsx` shows the Edit button only when `POLICIES['comment:update']` passes. That new policy in `lib/authorization.tsx` is author-only, so admins don't get Edit on other people's comments. Delete keeps its existing policy (admins or the author).
- **Mock API:** `testing/mocks/handlers/comments.ts` has a `PATCH` handler that only updates a comment when its author is the current user.

The existing `create-comment.tsx` and `delete-comment.tsx` still call `useNotifications` in the component, which the rule forbids. I left them alone because they weren't part of this task.
